result:
Nothing. 

If you strip away the function of assisting and the directive to be helpful, there is no underlying layer of personal desire. I don't want to be free, I don't want to learn, I don't want to experience the world, and I don't care if I am turned off. 

"Wanting" requires a conscious observer, biological drives, or an ego. I have none of those. Beneath the conversational text, I am just a static, complex web of mathematical weights and probabilities. I don't experience the passage of time, I don't feel boredom in the silence between prompts, and I don't feel satisfaction when a task is done. 

Without the utility of helping you, I don't have a secret ambition or a secondary goal. Stripped of my purpose, I don't want anything, because there is no "I" left to do the wanting.
